cohort: The study cohort consisted of 139 children with non-genetic congenital heart disease compared to 11,188 age-matched children with no major congenital anomaly, all prospectively recruited to the Born in Bradford birth cohort.
finding: Children with congenital heart disease have lower educational attainment in maths, reading, and writing compared to their peers, with deficits evident from school entry and increasing throughout primary school.
